scope_rule: PUBLIC-RECORD ONLY. Facts from Commissioner of Lobbying Registry, SEDAR corporate filings, Canada Gazette appointment notices, Ethics Commissioner reports, Elections Canada, on-the-record Canadian news coverage, and corporate registry. No speculation. Only documented business connections (revolving-door appointments, board seats, consultancy contracts, lobbying registrations, unregistered-lobbying findings) with explicit overlap to the actor's federal role.
note: 19th accountability axis. User-directed: 'find individuals and political business connections and links of influence.' Focuses on Grover-marked decision-makers with documented corporate/lobbying/board connections that predate, overlap, or post-date their federal role. Connection types: revolving_door (cabinet → corporate board), prior_corporate_role (corporate → cabinet), concurrent_board_seat (while in office), post_cabinet_consulting, unregistered_lobbying_finding. Each entry cites the primary source.
primary_sources: Commissioner of Lobbying of Canada Registry (lobbycanada.gc.ca)
Office of the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner reports
On-the-record Canadian news coverage (CBC, Globe, Star, Post, La Presse, CP)

marked_actors.name: Bill Morneau
marked_actors.business_connection: Morneau Shepell Inc. — Executive Chairman until Nov 2015; family firm (one of Canada's largest human-resources consulting firms, renamed LifeWorks in 2021, acquired by Telus Health in 2022)
marked_actors.overlap_finding: Morneau II Report by Ethics Commissioner Mario Dion (Feb 2021) found Morneau violated Conflict of Interest Act s.9 re: WE Charity contract administration. Prior French-villa disclosure lapse resulted in $200 penalty (Canada Gazette 2017). Family-firm pension-law legislation (Bill C-27) during his tenure was also scrutinized.
primary_sources: Canada Gazette Ethics Commissioner penalty notice 2017

marked_actors.name: Mark Carney
marked_actors.federal_role: Governor of the Bank of Canada 2008-2013; subsequent Canadian political candidate 2025
marked_actors.business_connection: Brookfield Asset Management — Vice Chair + Head of ESG and Impact Fund Investing 2020-2024 (~C$6.8M disclosed stock options at entry, per media reports). Chair of Bloomberg Sustainable Markets Initiative. United Nations Special Envoy on Climate Action and Finance 2019-2024.
marked_actors.overlap_finding: Entered Liberal Party leadership race Jan 2025; became PM March 2025. The Brookfield/Carney dossier (data/carney_brookfield_dossier.json, Merkle 9dcd8def37b9d98b) documents the overlapping private-sector-to-federal-executive transition. Governor of England (Bank of England 2013-2020) during Brexit. Concurrent-axis analysis: both 'carney' and 'central_banking' Grover axes.

marked_actors.name: Scott Brison
marked_actors.federal_role: President of the Treasury Board 2015-2019 (Phoenix Pay launch era)
marked_actors.business_connection: BMO Capital Markets — Vice Chair, Investment & Corporate Banking (2019-present). Appointed directly from Cabinet.
marked_actors.overlap_finding: Phoenix Pay System was launched during his Treasury Board presidency Feb 2016; persistent backlog (~110k cases as of 2024 per PSAC tally). Moved directly to BMO Capital Markets upon leaving Cabinet Jan 2019 — textbook revolving-door case.
primary_sources: BMO Capital Markets leadership announcement Feb 2019
Treasury Board of Canada President-of-Treasury-Board public record

marked_actors.name: David MacNaughton
marked_actors.federal_role: Canadian Ambassador to the United States 2016-2019 (appointed by Trudeau)
marked_actors.business_connection: Palantir Technologies Canada — Appointed President 2019 directly from ambassadorship.
marked_actors.overlap_finding: Commissioner of Lobbying Nancy Bélanger investigation found David MacNaughton violated the Lobbying Act by engaging in unregistered lobbying while President of Palantir Canada — the report was delivered April 2021 to Parliament. Subsequent 5-year prohibition on lobbying. Textbook post-cabinet ambassador-to-US-tech-contractor revolving-door case.
primary_sources: Commissioner of Lobbying report to Parliament April 2021
Canadian Ambassador to US public record
The Globe and Mail reporting on the lobbying finding 2021

marked_actors.name: Navdeep Bains
marked_actors.federal_role: Minister of Innovation, Science and Industry 2015-2021
marked_actors.business_connection: CIBC — Vice Chair, Strategic Client Coverage (2021-present). Joined CIBC April 2021 after leaving Cabinet January 2021.
marked_actors.overlap_finding: Innovation portfolio covered CIBC-regulatory-intersecting files (financial-technology regulation, federal science funding). Moved directly from Cabinet to major Canadian bank — a revolving-door pattern parallel to Scott Brison → BMO.

marked_actors.name: John Manley
marked_actors.federal_role: Deputy Prime Minister + Minister of Finance 2002-2003 (Chrétien government)
marked_actors.business_connection: Business Council of Canada — President and CEO 2010-2018; subsequently board positions at multiple major Canadian corporations (CIBC, CAE, Telus), and Senior Business Advisor at Bennett Jones LLP. Historical revolving-door-to-board template.
marked_actors.overlap_finding: Post-cabinet template for Canadian federal → major-corporate-advocacy transition. Business Council of Canada is Canada's primary corporate-public-policy advocacy organization.
primary_sources: Business Council of Canada leadership history
Bennett Jones LLP senior business advisor record
Corporations Canada director filings for CIBC, CAE, Telus

marked_actors.name: Stephen Harper
marked_actors.business_connection: Harper & Associates Consulting — founded 2016 directly after leaving office. Chairman of the International Democracy Union 2018-present. Various corporate board positions.
marked_actors.overlap_finding: Immediate post-PM transition to consulting while retaining public platform. IDU role provides ongoing global political-advisor-to-industry positioning.

marked_actors.name: Frank McKenna
marked_actors.federal_role: Canadian Ambassador to the United States 2005-2006; previously Premier of New Brunswick 1987-1997
marked_actors.business_connection: TD Bank — Deputy Chair since 2006 (near-continuous for ~20 years). Multiple board positions including CanaccordGenuity.
marked_actors.overlap_finding: Longest-tenured Canadian federal-political-to-major-bank revolving-door role — 20+ years as TD Bank Deputy Chair. Sets the template for the Brison/Bains moves.
primary_sources: Government of Canada ambassadorial appointment history

marked_actors.name: Dominic Barton
marked_actors.federal_role: Canadian Ambassador to China 2019-2021 (McKinsey-contract controversy era)
marked_actors.business_connection: Global Managing Partner, McKinsey & Company 2009-2018 (immediately pre-ambassadorship); subsequently Chair of Rio Tinto 2022-present, Chair of LeapFrog Investments. Chair of the Canadian federal Advisory Council on Economic Growth 2016-2017.
marked_actors.overlap_finding: McKinsey federal-contract reporting by The Canadian Press and AG (2023 Report) found McKinsey federal contracts grew from ~$2M/year pre-2015 to ~$117M cumulative 2015-2022 — the period overlapping with Barton's Advisory Council leadership and subsequent ambassadorship. Barton personally denies involvement in individual contract decisions.
primary_sources: Auditor General of Canada 2023 Report on McKinsey federal contracts
Canadian federal Advisory Council on Economic Growth terms of reference 2016

marked_actors.name: Gerald Butts
marked_actors.federal_role: Principal Secretary to Prime Minister Justin Trudeau 2015-2019 (resigned during SNC-Lavalin affair)
marked_actors.business_connection: Eurasia Group — Vice Chairman (2020-present). Previously WWF-Canada President 2008-2012 (pre-PMO).
marked_actors.overlap_finding: Post-PMO transition to global-policy-consulting Eurasia Group, aligned with global climate/geopolitics policy positioning. Jody Wilson-Raybould's sworn testimony (Feb 2019) named Butts in the SNC-Lavalin pressure chain.

marked_actors.name: Katie Telford
marked_actors.federal_role: Chief of Staff to Prime Minister Justin Trudeau 2015-2025
marked_actors.business_connection: Publicly-disclosed concurrent advisory/board positions under Ethics Commissioner spouse/conjugal-partner disclosure rules (spouse Robert Silver held senior role at The Winnipeg Free Press). Post-2025 positioning to be documented.
marked_actors.overlap_finding: Longest-tenured PMO Chief of Staff in Canadian federal history (10 years). Appeared before House committees re: SNC-Lavalin, China interference, WE Charity. Future post-PMO role highly relevant to revolving-door tracking.

marked_actors.name: Morris Rosenberg
marked_actors.federal_role: Deputy Minister of Health 2004-2010, Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs 2010-2013
marked_actors.business_connection: Author of the federal Public Inquiry Commission into Foreign Interference preliminary report 2023. Previously Senior Advisor at Bennett Jones LLP.
marked_actors.overlap_finding: Selected by federal government to author the initial independent report on the 2019/2021 election foreign interference matter (March 2023). Report's scope and limits were subsequently scrutinized when the Hogue Commission was called. Public-inquiry architecture overlap with foreign_interference axis.
primary_sources: Bennett Jones LLP senior advisor record

axis_summary.scope_discipline: PUBLIC-RECORD ONLY · documented business connections only · overlap-required with federal role
axis_summary.key_structural_finding: The Canadian federal accountability system distinguishes between lobbying registration (Commissioner of Lobbying) and post-cabinet activity (Lobbying Act 5-year cooling-off), but has no designated oversight body for the pattern of revolving-door transitions as a whole. The Brison-to-BMO, Bains-to-CIBC, McKenna-to-TD, Butts-to-Eurasia, MacNaughton-to-Palantir pattern is individually reviewed by the Commissioner of Lobbying where lobbying occurs, but the aggregate revolving-door pattern itself is not the scope of any single oversight body — same structural gap identified in the spouse/family axis.
